title: 07. Unsupervised Learning: Unsupervised Learning — runnable code
summary: Unsupervised Learning — runnable code: Generate synthetic data with 3 clusters; Find optimal k using elbow method.

sections.title: Example 1: K-Means Clustering
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 1: K-Means Clustering")
print("-" * 50)

# Generate synthetic data with 3 clusters
X_blobs, y_true = make_blobs(
    n_samples=300, centers=3, cluster_std=0.60, random_state=42
)

# Find optimal k using elbow method
inertias = []
silhouette_scores = []
k_range = range(2, 11)

for k in k_range:
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    kmeans.fit(X_blobs)
    inertias.append(kmeans.inertia_)
    silhouette_scores.append(silhouette_score(X_blobs, kmeans.labels_))

# Plot elbow curve
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 5))

ax1.plot(k_range, inertias, "bo-")
ax1.set_xlabel("Number of Clusters (k)")
ax1.set_ylabel("Inertia")
ax1.set_title("Elbow Method for Optimal k")
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

ax2.plot(k_range, silhouette_scores, "ro-")
ax2.set_xlabel("Number of Clusters (k)")
ax2.set_ylabel("Silhouette Score")
ax2.set_title("Silhouette Score vs k")
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Optimal k from silhouette score
optimal_k = k_range[np.argmax(silhouette_scores)]
print(f"Optimal k from silhouette score: {optimal_k}")

# Train K-Means with optimal k
kmeans_optimal = KMeans(n_clusters=optimal_k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans_optimal.fit(X_blobs)
y_pred = kmeans_optimal.labels_

# Evaluate clustering
print(f"Silhouette Score: {silhouette_score(X_blobs, y_pred):.4f}")
print(f"Davies-Bouldin Index: {davies_bouldin_score(X_blobs, y_pred):.4f}")
print(f"Calinski-Harabasz Index: {calinski_harabasz_score(X_blobs, y_pred):.4f}")

# Visualize results
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 5))

plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.scatter(X_blobs[:, 0], X_blobs[:, 1], c=y_true, cmap="viridis", alpha=0.7)
plt.title("True Clusters")
plt.xlabel("Feature 1")
plt.ylabel("Feature 2")

plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.scatter(X_blobs[:, 0], X_blobs[:, 1], c=y_pred, cmap="viridis", alpha=0.7)
plt.scatter(
    kmeans_optimal.cluster_centers_[:, 0],
    kmeans_optimal.cluster_centers_[:, 1],
    c="red",
    marker="x",
    s=200,
    linewidths=3,
    label="Centroids",
)
plt.title("K-Means Clustering Results")
plt.xlabel("Feature 1")
plt.ylabel("Feature 2")
plt.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Example 3: Dbscan Clustering
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 3: DBSCAN Clustering")
print("-" * 50)

# Generate data with non-spherical clusters
X_moons, y_moons = make_moons(n_samples=200, noise=0.1, random_state=42)
X_circles, y_circles = make_circles(
    n_samples=200, noise=0.1, factor=0.5, random_state=42
)

# Combine datasets
X_complex = np.vstack([X_moons, X_circles + [3, 0]])
y_complex = np.hstack([y_moons, y_circles + 2])

# Apply DBSCAN
dbscan = DBSCAN(eps=0.3, min_samples=5)
y_pred_dbscan = dbscan.fit_predict(X_complex)

# Evaluate clustering
n_clusters_dbscan = len(set(y_pred_dbscan)) - (1 if -1 in y_pred_dbscan else 0)
n_noise = list(y_pred_dbscan).count(-1)

print(f"Estimated number of clusters: {n_clusters_dbscan}")
print(f"Estimated number of noise points: {n_noise}")
print(f"Silhouette Score: {silhouette_score(X_complex, y_pred_dbscan):.4f}")

# Visualize results
plt.figure(figsize=(15, 5))

plt.subplot(1, 3, 1)
plt.scatter(X_complex[:, 0], X_complex[:, 1], c=y_complex, cmap="viridis", alpha=0.7)
plt.title("True Clusters")
plt.xlabel("Feature 1")
plt.ylabel("Feature 2")

plt.subplot(1, 3, 2)
plt.scatter(
    X_complex[:, 0], X_complex[:, 1], c=y_pred_dbscan, cmap="viridis", alpha=0.7
)
plt.title("DBSCAN Clustering")
plt.xlabel("Feature 1")
plt.ylabel("Feature 2")

# Compare with K-Means
kmeans_complex = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10)
y_pred_kmeans = kmeans_complex.fit_predict(X_complex)

plt.subplot(1, 3, 3)
plt.scatter(
    X_complex[:, 0], X_complex[:, 1], c=y_pred_kmeans, cmap="viridis", alpha=0.7
)
plt.title("K-Means Clustering")
plt.xlabel("Feature 1")
plt.ylabel("Feature 2")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Example 4: Principal Component Analysis (Pca)
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 4: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)")
print("-" * 50)

# Use digits dataset
digits = load_digits()
X_digits = digits.data
y_digits = digits.target

# Apply PCA
pca = PCA()
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_digits)

# Plot explained variance ratio
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 5))

plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.plot(
    range(1, len(pca.explained_variance_ratio_) + 1),
    np.cumsum(pca.explained_variance_ratio_),
    "bo-",
)
plt.xlabel("Number of Components")
plt.ylabel("Cumulative Explained Variance Ratio")
plt.title("Explained Variance vs Number of Components")
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.bar(range(1, 11), pca.explained_variance_ratio_[:10])
plt.xlabel("Principal Component")
plt.ylabel("Explained Variance Ratio")
plt.title("First 10 Principal Components")
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Choose number of components (explain 95% of variance)
n_components_95 = np.argmax(np.cumsum(pca.explained_variance_ratio_) >= 0.95) + 1
print(f"Number of components to explain 95% variance: {n_components_95}")

# Apply PCA with selected components
pca_95 = PCA(n_components=n_components_95)
X_pca_95 = pca_95.fit_transform(X_digits)

print(f"Original dimensions: {X_digits.shape[1]}")
print(f"Reduced dimensions: {X_pca_95.shape[1]}")
print(f"Variance explained: {np.sum(pca_95.explained_variance_ratio_):.4f}")

# Visualize first 2 principal components
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
scatter = plt.scatter(X_pca[:, 0], X_pca[:, 1], c=y_digits, cmap="tab10", alpha=0.7)
plt.xlabel("First Principal Component")
plt.ylabel("Second Principal Component")
plt.title("Digits Dataset - First 2 Principal Components")
plt.colorbar(scatter)
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Example 6: Association Rule Learning (Apriori-style)
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 6: Association Rule Learning")
print("-" * 50)

# Create synthetic market basket data
np.random.seed(42)
n_transactions = 1000
products = ["bread", "milk", "eggs", "butter", "cheese", "yogurt", "apples", "bananas"]

# Generate transactions
transactions = []
for _ in range(n_transactions):
    # Random number of products per transaction (1-4)
    n_items = np.random.randint(1, 5)
    transaction = np.random.choice(products, size=n_items, replace=False)
    transactions.append(list(transaction))

# Convert to one-hot encoded format
from mlxtend.preprocessing import TransactionEncoder
from mlxtend.frequent_patterns import apriori, association_rules

te = TransactionEncoder()
te_ary = te.fit(transactions).transform(transactions)
df_transactions = pd.DataFrame(te_ary, columns=te.columns_)

# Find frequent itemsets
frequent_itemsets = apriori(df_transactions, min_support=0.1, use_colnames=True)

print("Frequent Itemsets:")
print(frequent_itemsets.head(10))

# Generate association rules
rules = association_rules(frequent_itemsets, metric="confidence", min_threshold=0.5)

print("\nAssociation Rules:")
print(rules.head(10))

# Visualize support vs confidence
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.scatter(rules["support"], rules["confidence"], alpha=0.7)
plt.xlabel("Support")
plt.ylabel("Confidence")
plt.title("Association Rules: Support vs Confidence")
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Example 7: Customer Segmentation with Multiple Algorithms
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 7: Customer Segmentation")
print("-" * 50)

# Generate customer data
np.random.seed(42)
n_customers = 500
customer_data = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "age": np.random.normal(35, 10, n_customers),
        "income": np.random.lognormal(10, 0.5, n_customers),
        "spending_score": np.random.uniform(1, 100, n_customers),
        "purchase_frequency": np.random.poisson(5, n_customers),
        "avg_order_value": np.random.exponential(50, n_customers),
    }
)

# Add some patterns to create segments
customer_data.loc[customer_data["income"] > 60000, "spending_score"] *= 1.5
customer_data.loc[customer_data["age"] > 50, "purchase_frequency"] *= 0.7

# Scale features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_customers_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(customer_data)

# Apply different clustering algorithms
algorithms = {
    "K-Means": KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10),
    "Hierarchical": AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=4),
    "DBSCAN": DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5),
}

results = {}
for name, algorithm in algorithms.items():
    if name == "DBSCAN":
        labels = algorithm.fit_predict(X_customers_scaled)
        n_clusters = len(set(labels)) - (1 if -1 in labels else 0)
    else:
        labels = algorithm.fit_predict(X_customers_scaled)
        n_clusters = len(set(labels))

    silhouette = silhouette_score(X_customers_scaled, labels)
    results[name] = {
        "labels": labels,
        "n_clusters": n_clusters,
        "silhouette": silhouette,
    }
    print(f"{name}: {n_clusters} clusters, Silhouette Score: {silhouette:.4f}")

# Visualize results
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(15, 12))

# Original data
axes[0, 0].scatter(customer_data["age"], customer_data["income"], alpha=0.7)
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel("Age")
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("Income")
axes[0, 0].set_title("Original Customer Data")

# K-Means results
axes[0, 1].scatter(
    customer_data["age"],
    customer_data["income"],
    c=results["K-Means"]["labels"],
    cmap="viridis",
    alpha=0.7,
)
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel("Age")
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel("Income")
axes[0, 1].set_title("K-Means Clustering")

# Hierarchical results
axes[1, 0].scatter(
    customer_data["age"],
    customer_data["income"],
    c=results["Hierarchical"]["labels"],
    cmap="viridis",
    alpha=0.7,
)
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel("Age")
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("Income")
axes[1, 0].set_title("Hierarchical Clustering")

# DBSCAN results
axes[1, 1].scatter(
    customer_data["age"],
    customer_data["income"],
    c=results["DBSCAN"]["labels"],
    cmap="viridis",
    alpha=0.7,
)
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel("Age")
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel("Income")
axes[1, 1].set_title("DBSCAN Clustering")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Example 8: Dimensionality Reduction Comparison
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Exercise 1: K-Means Clustering for Customer Segmentation Create a customer segmentation model using K-Means clustering.
- Project 1: Customer Segmentation for E-commerce Process: 1.
- Unsupervised learning discovers hidden patterns without labeled data 2.
- Use a more complex dataset
- Apply different dimensionality reduction techniques
- Original 3D data (first 2 dimensions)

```python
print("\nExample 8: Dimensionality Reduction Comparison")

# Use a more complex dataset
from sklearn.datasets import make_swiss_roll

X_swiss, color = make_swiss_roll(n_samples=1000, noise=0.2, random_state=42)

# Apply different dimensionality reduction techniques
# PCA
pca_swiss = PCA(n_components=2)
X_pca_swiss = pca_swiss.fit_transform(X_swiss)

# t-SNE
tsne_swiss = TSNE(n_components=2, random_state=42, perplexity=30)
X_tsne_swiss = tsne_swiss.fit_transform(X_swiss)

# Visualize results
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(15, 5))

# Original 3D data (first 2 dimensions)
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(131)
scatter1 = ax1.scatter(X_swiss[:, 0], X_swiss[:, 1], c=color, cmap="viridis", alpha=0.7)
ax1.set_xlabel("X")
ax1.set_ylabel("Y")
ax1.set_title("Original Data (First 2 dimensions)")
plt.colorbar(scatter1, ax=ax1)

# PCA results
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(132)
scatter2 = ax2.scatter(
    X_pca_swiss[:, 0], X_pca_swiss[:, 1], c=color, cmap="viridis", alpha=0.7
)
ax2.set_xlabel("First Principal Component")
ax2.set_ylabel("Second Principal Component")
ax2.set_title("PCA")
plt.colorbar(scatter2, ax=ax2)

# t-SNE results
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(133)
scatter3 = ax3.scatter(
    X_tsne_swiss[:, 0], X_tsne_swiss[:, 1], c=color, cmap="viridis", alpha=0.7
)
ax3.set_xlabel("First t-SNE Component")
ax3.set_ylabel("Second t-SNE Component")
ax3.set_title("t-SNE")
plt.colorbar(scatter3, ax=ax3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
